faqs.0.question: Is borrowing against crypto a taxable event?
faqs.0.answer: In most jurisdictions no — drawing a loan is not a disposal, so no capital gains event is triggered. Selling collateral to repay, or a liquidation, can be a disposal.
faqs.1.question: What LTV do DeFi collateral cards use?
faqs.1.answer: Most expose 50–65% LTV on ETH-type collateral — more conservative than the protocol maximum (~80%) to leave headroom before liquidation.
faqs.2.question: What happens if my collateral gets liquidated?
faqs.2.answer: The protocol sells enough collateral to cover the debt plus a ~5–8% penalty. That partial forced sale can trigger a taxable disposal on the sold portion.
faqs.3.question: Which crypto cards use DeFi collateral?
faqs.3.answer: ether.fi Cash, Exa, Ethena Pay and other card rails that settle from self-custodied or staked positions rather than a custodial fiat balance.
body.oe8whz7: Collateralized crypto cards borrow a stablecoin credit line against your on-chain position at the moment you spend. Because borrowing is not a disposal, the spend does not realize capital gains in most jurisdictions — you repay later while the collateral keeps earning yield.
body.u4zq7eu: The Mechanics of Over-Collateralized Borrowing for Everyday Purchases
body.4t3736x: A DeFi collateral card works like a credit line that draws on your posted collateral when you tap to pay. The merchant gets fiat; you get a growing debt position denominated in stablecoins, with interest accruing on the debt — not on the underlying asset, which stays earning.

body.3baqfl6: Aave v3 — ETH/wstETH: ~80% max LTV, ~5% liquidation penalty, credit in USDC/USDT/DAI. Stablecoin collateral: ~93% LTV. Compound v3 — ETH/wstETH: ~82% LTV, ~5–8% penalty, USDC credit. Card rails typically expose a more conservative 50–65% LTV to leave headroom.

body.3dljqv3: Tax Efficiency: Why Borrowing Beats Disposing of Assets
body.q00ufwa: Selling crypto to spend creates a taxable disposal in most jurisdictions — you realize the gain in that moment. Borrowing against it does not: a loan is not a disposal, so no capital gains event is triggered when you draw the credit line. The trade-off is interest plus liquidation risk instead of a tax bill.

body.g6ko4dv: UK — disposal only when collateral is sold or the loan is settled in kind
body.0lhqks5: EU — generally no disposal on borrowing; confirm local MiCA member-state rules
body.t24t3jl: Canada — borrowing not taxable; liquidation may trigger a disposal on the sold portion

body.6vno4az: If your collateral value falls and the health factor drops toward 1.0, the protocol liquidates enough collateral to cover the debt. That partial forced sale can itself be a taxable disposal — the scenario borrowing was meant to avoid.
body.cygjaw9: Keep health factor above ~1.5–2.0 in volatile conditions
